newsitem.title: ITALY: EU's Monti sure Italy to try hard for deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: EU's Monti sure Italy to try hard for deficit goal.

text.p: European Commissioner Mario Monti said he was confident the Italian government would not stint in trying to reach a target ratio this year of three percent deficit to gross domestic product (GDP).
"I am confident the government will not grudge the efforts needed either in intensity or timing to achieve the three percent deficit objective in 1997 and in 1998," Monti said.

Talking to reporters in Venice he said as far as the need for a possible Italian mini-budget for this year was concerned, "it is important that the budget is for all the measures necessary to achieve the stated objective of a three percent deficit (to GDP ratio) in 1997."

Asked if a mini-budget should be carried out in spring, he replied: "For every action of this kind, the sooner it is done the less painful and the less dear it is because the benefits mature sooner, like confidence in terms of lower interest rates that the markets have shown they give in response to good economic policy measures."
